newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil in 'no hurry' to sell CVRD - paper.
newsitem.headline: Brazil in 'no hurry' to sell CVRD - paper.

text.p: The Brazilian government is in no hurry to sell mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) and reports of new gold and copper deposits could slow its privatization, O Estado de Sao Paulo said.

The paper, citing an interview with Luiz Carlos Mendonca de Barros, president of Brazil's National Development Bank (BNDES), said transparency would determine the pace of the CVRD selloff, which the government hopes to carry out in the first quarter.
"We have a process under way now that is free of ethical or judicial questions and that is what is most important," Mendonca de Barros told the paper.
Officials in Brasilia have so far denied reports that new gold and copper finds -- whose sizes are still not clear -- could delay the CVRD auction to re-evaluate its worth.

But Estado said Mendonca de Barros raised the possibility of an auction delay by suggesting that the need for transparency in dealing with the new finds was a priority that could slow the privatization process.
"In the case of (CVRD) the need for transparency will determine the velocity of the privatization," Mendonca de Barros was quoted as saying.
He did not say whether the new deposits would prevent the government from going ahead with plans to sell off CVRD this quarter. The company is expected to fetch at least $8.0 billion.
